# commit create --fill uses an external command to edit the message.

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2026-11-06T20:00:00Z'

mkdir repo
cd repo
git init
git commit --allow-empty -m Initial
gs repo init
gs branch create feature --no-commit

# A command is required only when a message needs filling.
! gs commit create --fill --allow-empty
stderr 'spice.message.fill.command'
gs commit create --fill --allow-empty -m 'Supplied without command'

git config spice.message.fill.command mock-message
env MOCK_MESSAGE_RESPONSE=$WORK/message.txt
env MOCK_MESSAGE_RECORD=$WORK/invocation

gs commit create --fill --allow-empty
stdout 'Generator progress'
stderr 'Generator diagnostic'
grep '^commit-create$' $WORK/invocation/operation
git log -1 --format=%B
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/message.txt

# Fixup messages bypass the command.
env MOCK_MESSAGE_EXIT=8
gs commit create --allow-empty --fill --fixup HEAD
git log -1 --format=%s
stdout '^fixup! Generated subject$'

# Configured filling can be disabled for one invocation.
env MOCK_MESSAGE_EXIT=
git config spice.message.fill true
gs commit create --allow-empty
git log -1 --format=%s
stdout '^Generated subject$'
env MOCK_MESSAGE_EXIT=8
gs commit amend --no-fill --no-edit --allow-empty

-- golden/message.txt --
Generated subject

Generated body

-- message.txt --
Generated subject

Generated body
